<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by pinning A to the live comparison: whether spreading actually replaces the funnel or merely adds a flexible remainder while Saturday stays packed. A built a coherent managed-redistribution case and was more careful on substitution, but retreated to an unquantified slice, conceded peaks may remain full, and never showed that remainder converts overload enough to justify naming new districts. B’s hub-management alternative and “wrong remainder / extra stop” frame gave the cleaner vote reason.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s remainder attack (flexible visitors are not the peak packers; Saturday stays full while Tuesday gets a new crowd), locked in after A conceded no share and that Saturday may remain booked.</best_rebuttal>
